items.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023
items.q: what about Jack Teagarden, what about Jimmy Rodgers, what about Elvis Presley? Those people all had a right to sing the blues I think.

ctx.x: That was Ed’s point also that I’m referring to it, the process of — a verb.

The music swings or it doesn’t swing. Bluegrass can swing but swing is not its, that’s not where the music starts from. It’s not jazz music. It’s music where basically out of the Virginia, West Virginia, Kentucky, Tennessee, that little quadrant of — a quadrant — because actually it’s five states down there in that little nexus around Bristol, Virginia where Jimmy Rodgers and the Carter family kind of — they didn’t define modern country music but they kind of set down some informal barriers as to what hillbilly…

that you couldn’t play according to that rhythm. When jukeboxes came around in the 1930s all of a sudden you needed string basses for more than just big dance bands. You had to have string basses so the people could dance into taverns where there were only jukeboxes and they couldn’t hear the beat unless the jukebox record had a bass on it. That’s where the basses come from according to me.
